transcript.text: Magic is probably the strongest combat style in all of RuneScape Dragon Isles and in this video, I'll go over not only
why it's so strong, but how to level it quickly, what unlocks you'll get along the way, and the best gear for you to
wear no matter what stage of the game you're currently at. But, let's go ahead and start out by talking about the
different unlocks that you'll get at each level and what they actually do. To start out at level one, you will have
the ability to use air magic spells. You'll also unlock the base 0.5% reduced stamina consumption when attacking with
magic weapons perk, which you'll also get for every single level you gain, which maxes out at 49.5%
once you reach level 99. Next, you'll unlock secondary attacks once you reach level five, which allows
you to charge up your weapon and release a powerful secondary staff spell. Following that is water magic, which is
a new damage type that somethings are weak to, but more importantly allows you to heal yourself with it by using its
special attack. It also has a chance for when you kill enemies to spawn small water orbs on the ground, which you can
also pick up for some additional healing. At level 11, you'll unlock the surge spell, which allows you to dodge
further distances without consuming too much stamina. At level 16, you'll get arcane
expertise, which unlocks an additional powerful magic attack at the end of your staff magic combo. For an example, you
could use water magic to cause a tidal wave as your final attack in the combo. At level 20, you'll get runic refund,
which simply gives you a 30% chance not to consume runes when attacking with magic. At level 21, you'll finally
unlock fire magic, which is arguably the best type of damage that you can do in the game, since it also applies a
burning debuff to enemies, giving you some extra damage. At level 25, you'll get afterimage,
which is incredibly powerful, as this makes it so when you use your surge ability, you'll now be able to leave
behind a illusionary image that will absorb some attacks from enemies buying you time to run, hide, or just get some
more damage off. At level 30, you will unlock confuse which allows you to turn lesser enemies to your side so they
fight for you and once again start tanking enemies so you don't have to. At level 34, you'll unlock the magic
potion which just gives you a little bit of a buff for your damage. At level 39, you get the magic focus
which again essentially does the exact same thing. At level 44, you'll get greater confuse
which now allows you to confuse a much wider variety of creatures and bring them to your side. In particular, this
is usable on much more powerful enemies so you can very easily turn the tide of battle rather than simply having to use
it on the weakest thing nearby. At level 61, you get enfeeble which is one of the newer spells they've added to
magic which allows you to weaken the target opponent so that they hit for less damage. This is again extremely
useful on elite enemies but use it however you like. Then at level 80, we get vengeance which
allows you to reflect the next incoming attack back at your enemies. I highly recommend activating this before you
start any challenging fight but just know in my personal opinion, it's extremely strong.
And finally at level 99, you get the ever infamous magic skill cape. So with that all out of the way, let's go ahead
and jump into your actual leveling process and how to level up magic as efficiently as possible. When it comes
to leveling up the skill, you'll probably want to start out by using your magic air attacks on things that you can
find throughout Rellekka and Misthalin at least until you unlock fire spells at level 21. If you can, it's important to
note that from here on out you should make sure that you always have the knowledge is power buff which provides
you with 10% extra XP not only for magic but anything else that you do. If you don't know, there is a wide variety of
food that you can obtain this from, such as the glazed pumpkin sandwich, sweet veg roll, and wild pie. Once you unlock
fire magic, you should start using it pretty much immediately since it does a burn effect, further increasing your
damage. The fastest place to level up inside Bramble Me Valley is probably going to be at any one of the local
goblin camps that you can find. But, to be honest with you, just kill things as you progress throughout the story in
this zone and you should reach around level 25 to 30 by the time you start moving on. Once you reach the fractured
plains biome, you will want to try and reach a bare minimum of level 39 before you try taking on the first boss inside
the tower. This is because you'll have your most important skills unlocked, such as after image, which keeps enemies
off of you, and the magic focus, as well as potion, which both increase your damage output. Next, you'll be heading
into Fell Hollow, which is where you can really start to farm a ton of XP. At this point, if you haven't already done
so, make sure to craft yourself an inspiring amulet of magic for a 5% XP buff to speed things along as the real
grind starts now. As you explore the zone, you'll start to notice large hordes of zombies in different areas.
You'll want to start out by using water spells with the strongest staff that you
currently have available. Next, go ahead and start collecting up all of the zombies in a group, creating a sort of
train behind you. Once you've gathered up a relatively large area, then you'll want to go ahead and start spamming your
combo attack as the tidal wave hits all of them for a massive amount of AoE damage, giving you some of the fastest
levels possible and making it so they don't have to be perfectly grouped up like they would be if you were using
fire spells. I personally recommend that you stay here until you reach level 80 as it is arguably the fastest way to
level up in the entire game. The next best option, however, is farming Cal fights inside the Umbral Sands biome
later on as you start to approach the end game. This is either on par or slightly faster even than farming
zombies as you'll have more powerful weapons and they have more HP for you to burn through. But until then, I still
recommend you stick with zombies. The best place to farm the Cal fights, however, will probably be at these spots
which you can set up a loadstone to and jump between different groups while the other ones respond. Now, let's go ahead
and move on to talking about the best gear available in the very beginning, early, mid, and late game that you can
use. For the beginning of the game, you'll want to try and get either the oak wand or oak battle staff as soon as
possible. The best gear available at this point will simply be the wizard hat, wizard robes, and wizard robe legs.
For the early game, which means prior to defeating the first boss, but once you're past Bramble Meet Valley, you'll
want to go for either the Dragon Kin Mage armor set or the Dark Mage armor set, whichever you personally prefer. To
be honest though, these basically have the same stats, so just go for whatever's faster and easier for you to
get. For your necklace, you'll probably want to stick to the inspiring amulet of magic as it also provides a 5% XP boost
whenever you're trying to level from here on out. And for your weapon, you'll want to go ahead and run the staff of
light as it is arguably one of, if not the very best raw damage staff in the entire game. If you don't know how to
get that, consider checking out our staff guide as it'll go over how to unlock each of these different weapons
that we'll talk about throughout this video. In the mid game, you'll want to run the mystic hat, robes, and robe legs
as they have, again, the highest stats available along with the staff of light. Just make sure that you power it up as
often as you can to keep it stronger than anything else available at this point. For your necklace, you'll want to
run the amulet of magic for a 12.5% DPS increase. This is no joke and is definitely something you should actually
be running over the XP amulet as doing more damage means more XP and it's a higher amount than the 5% XP would give
you. When it comes to your cape, it's best to farm out the Zamorak cape since it will make your afterimages explode
for some extra damage. Finally, once you're moving into the end game, the best equipment available outside the
current raid gear is full infinity robes paired with the staff of light for damage and the Pharaoh's staff for the
special skill which spawns a scarab to tank enemies for you. Once again, if you don't know how to get this, please check
out our video as it goes over every staff that you can get up until the new raid. Now, when it comes to your cape
slot, there's an argument to be made for the fire cape, obsidian cape, and Zamorak cape depending on how you like
to play at this point. But, honestly, it doesn't really make too much of a difference which one you go with. As
you're playing throughout the game, magic simply won't be enough sometimes and you'll have to go into melee. And if
you want to learn more about that skill and how to level it quickly, consider checking out this video.

comments.text:
I would humbly submit that air magic is king, in general. Air attacks faster anyways (with full magic set it’s even faster), causes a small stun with normal attacks and can knock down enemies; and its final attack is a cone of damage that is GREAT for getting enemies in a line (which is easy to do when kiting). So far the only time I break out fire is if I’m safe spotting a zogre. 

Air does the highest damage to dragons too, including velger (still need to test on imaru, but I’m certain it’s the same.)

Fire has powerful spells but a lot of enemies won’t stand still for the big 5,6,7 strikes, cause they’ve closed the gap already and now you have to dodge and won’t get that combo. Air keeps most stuff away, does faster and more damage, and crowd control. 

Humbly submitted, I thank Yee for thou considering.

Edit: I will add now, that I think air magic may be king for new players getting the hang of combat in the game. Eventually you’ll get fluent in changing magic types depending on enemy weak weakness. Personally air magic felt the best when trying to level, as it gave me the most room to battle; now that I’ve played enough I rely less on that mechanic and utilize more spells and damage types. But, just have fun with it. As rule of cool goes, fire magic is king and has the most satisfying attacks.

comments.author: @slysilence
comments.text: Enfeeble & Vengeance should NOT be late game upgrades. Enfeeble would be way more useful if you got it much earlier. Honestly it should be one of the first skills to help keep the mage alive. Literally no one uses this skill consistently in late game. And why is Vengeance a magic skill? Mage’s want to avoid damage, not seek it. The Melee characters need this skill way more and they would need it much earlier. Magic capstone skills should be large AOE upgrades to confusion, enfeeble and elemental spells. Mages should use enfeeble & confusion to defend and use elemental damage for weakness and damage over time. Archery should get the dash clone skill and stealth skills to defend and fast high damage single target skills to kill things before they get too close. Melee should use tanking as attacking with vengeance or some kind of thorns damage to help kill things that come too close. These 3 play styles would work much more harmoniously with each. Not get in each other’s way while shoring up each Archetypes shortcomings. Just my option.
